title: The Weather Chart with One Blank Tuesday
sentences: The science class recorded the weather at eight every morning for two weeks.
They made a wall chart, and Tuesday of the second week was blank.
Monday was sunny and Wednesday cloudy, but neither proved Tuesday's weather.
Ryo checked the class notebook and found that the student on duty had been absent Tuesday.
The class did not fill the blank by copying a nearby day.
They looked for another school record from the same time.
The garden club had written 'light rain at 8:00' on its watering sheet that Tuesday.
The class added light rain to the chart and wrote 'garden club record' below the entry.
Ryo learned to fill a missing record with evidence, not a nearby-day guess.

slashRows.en: The science class recorded the weather at eight every morning for two weeks.
slashRows.jp: 理科のクラスは二週間、毎朝八時に天気を記録しました。

slashRows.en: They made a wall chart, and Tuesday of the second week was blank.
slashRows.jp: 壁の表を作ると、二週目の火曜日だけ空白でした。

slashRows.en: Monday was sunny and Wednesday cloudy, but neither proved Tuesday's weather.
slashRows.jp: 月曜は晴れ、水曜は曇りでしたが、どちらも火曜の天気を証明しませんでした。

slashRows.en: Ryo checked the class notebook and found that the student on duty had been absent Tuesday.
slashRows.jp: 亮がクラスノートを調べると、火曜日の係の生徒が欠席していたと分かりました。

slashRows.en: The class did not fill the blank by copying a nearby day.
slashRows.jp: クラスは前後の日を写して空欄を埋めませんでした。

slashRows.en: They looked for another school record from the same time.
slashRows.jp: 同じ時刻の別の学校記録がないか調べました。

slashRows.en: The garden club had written 'light rain at 8:00' on its watering sheet that Tuesday.
slashRows.jp: 園芸部はその火曜日の水やり表に「8時、小雨」と書いていました。

slashRows.en: The class added light rain to the chart and wrote 'garden club record' below the entry.
slashRows.jp: クラスは表に小雨と加え、その下に「園芸部記録」と書きました。

slashRows.en: Ryo learned to fill a missing record with evidence, not a nearby-day guess.
slashRows.jp: 亮は、欠けた記録は前後の日の推測でなく証拠で補うと学びました。

title: The Classroom Plant Leaning toward the Window
sentences: A small classroom plant stood on a shelf near the back wall.
After one week, its top leaves leaned strongly toward the window on the left.
Mina wondered whether the plant was simply falling because one side was heavier.
She checked the pot and found it stable, while the new stems were bending toward the light.
She did not cut the leaning stems or tie them straight immediately.
The class turned the pot halfway around and marked its new position.
Three days later, the newest leaves had begun turning back toward the window.
They continued turning the pot a little each week so different sides received light.
Mina learned that changing one condition and observing later can test an idea without damaging the plant.

slashRows.en: A small classroom plant stood on a shelf near the back wall.
slashRows.jp: 小さな教室の植物が後ろの壁近くの棚に置かれていました。

slashRows.en: After one week, its top leaves leaned strongly toward the window on the left.
slashRows.jp: 一週間後、上の葉が左側の窓へ大きく傾いていました。

slashRows.en: Mina wondered whether the plant was simply falling because one side was heavier.
slashRows.jp: 美奈は、片側が重くて倒れかけているだけではないかと思いました。

slashRows.en: She checked the pot and found it stable, while the new stems were bending toward the light.
slashRows.jp: 鉢は安定しており、新しい茎が光の方向へ曲がっていることを確認しました。

slashRows.en: She did not cut the leaning stems or tie them straight immediately.
slashRows.jp: 傾いた茎をすぐ切ったり、まっすぐ縛ったりはしませんでした。

slashRows.en: The class turned the pot halfway around and marked its new position.
slashRows.jp: クラスは鉢を半回転させ、新しい向きを記録しました。

slashRows.en: Three days later, the newest leaves had begun turning back toward the window.
slashRows.jp: 三日後、最も新しい葉は再び窓の方へ向き始めました。

slashRows.en: They continued turning the pot a little each week so different sides received light.
slashRows.jp: さまざまな側が光を受けるよう、毎週少しずつ鉢を回すことにしました。

slashRows.en: Mina learned that changing one condition and observing later can test an idea without damaging the plant.
slashRows.jp: 美奈は、一つの条件を変えて後で観察すれば植物を傷つけず考えを確かめられると学びました。

title: A Club Badge Box with Two Different Sizes
sentences: The tennis club received a box of new cloth badges for its uniforms.
The box held small and large badges together.
The order sheet showed eight small and twelve large badges for twenty members.
Yuki first planned to hand them out from the box, risking wrong sizes.
She checked the uniform list, which already recorded each member's badge size.
The club separated the badges into two trays and labeled them S and L.
They counted eight in the S tray and twelve in the L tray before distribution.
Each member gave a name, and Yuki matched it with the size on the list.
The club learned that sorting by recorded size prevents mix-ups.

slashRows.en: The tennis club received a box of new cloth badges for its uniforms.
slashRows.jp: テニス部はユニフォーム用の新しい布バッジが入った箱を受け取りました。

slashRows.en: The box held small and large badges together.
slashRows.jp: 箱には小さいバッジと大きいバッジが一緒に入っていました。

slashRows.en: The order sheet showed eight small and twelve large badges for twenty members.
slashRows.jp: 注文表には二十人分として小八枚、大十二枚とありました。

slashRows.en: Yuki first planned to hand them out from the box, risking wrong sizes.
slashRows.jp: 由紀は最初箱からそのまま配ろうとし、サイズ違いの恐れがありました。

slashRows.en: She checked the uniform list, which already recorded each member's badge size.
slashRows.jp: そこで、各部員のバッジサイズが記録されているユニフォーム表を確認しました。

slashRows.en: The club separated the badges into two trays and labeled them S and L.
slashRows.jp: 部はバッジを二つのトレーに分け、SとLの表示を付けました。

slashRows.en: They counted eight in the S tray and twelve in the L tray before distribution.
slashRows.jp: 配る前にSが八枚、Lが十二枚あることを数えました。

slashRows.en: Each member gave a name, and Yuki matched it with the size on the list.
slashRows.jp: 各部員が名前を言い、由紀が表のサイズと照合しました。

slashRows.en: The club learned that sorting by recorded size prevents mix-ups.
slashRows.jp: 部は、記録されたサイズで先に分けると取り違えを防げると学びました。

title: The Two Gloves That Did Not Make a Pair
sentences: After a cold morning, the lost-item box held two black gloves.
They looked similar from far away, so Taku put them together as one pair.
He picked them up and saw that both were left-hand gloves.
One had three gray lines at the wrist, while the other had a small red thread near the thumb.
Taku did not pair them just because their color matched.
He placed each glove separately and added a note about the place.
Later, one student described the gray lines and another described the red thread.
Each student received one glove and continued looking for its true partner.
Taku learned to check side and details before pairing similar lost items.

slashRows.en: After a cold morning, the lost-item box held two black gloves.
slashRows.jp: 寒い朝の後、落とし物箱には二つの黒い手袋が入っていました。

slashRows.en: They looked similar from far away, so Taku put them together as one pair.
slashRows.jp: 遠くからは似て見えたため、拓は一組として並べました。

slashRows.en: He picked them up and saw that both were left-hand gloves.
slashRows.jp: 手に取ると、どちらも左手用だと分かりました。

slashRows.en: One had three gray lines at the wrist, while the other had a small red thread near the thumb.
slashRows.jp: 一つは手首に灰色の線が三本あり、もう一つは親指近くに小さな赤い糸がありました。

slashRows.en: Taku did not pair them just because their color matched.
slashRows.jp: 拓は色が同じだけでは一組にしませんでした。

slashRows.en: He placed each glove separately and added a note about the place.
slashRows.jp: それぞれの手袋を別に置き、見つかった場所のメモを付けました。

slashRows.en: Later, one student described the gray lines and another described the red thread.
slashRows.jp: 後で一人の生徒が灰色の線を、別の生徒が赤い糸を説明しました。

slashRows.en: Each student received one glove and continued looking for its true partner.
slashRows.jp: それぞれが一つの手袋を受け取り、本当の片方を探し続けました。

slashRows.en: Taku learned to check side and details before pairing similar lost items.
slashRows.jp: 拓は、似た落とし物を組にする前に左右と細部を確認すると学びました。

title: A Hallway Display Put Up One Day Too Early
sentences: The art club prepared a hallway display for a Friday school event.
On Wednesday, a student read the calendar quickly and thought the event was Thursday.
The club put all the pictures on the hallway wall that afternoon.
A teacher then pointed out that another class needed the wall for a Thursday morning presentation.
The club checked the event calendar and confirmed Friday as its display date.
They did not ask the other class to change its scheduled presentation.
They removed the pictures, numbered their order, and stored them overnight.
After the Thursday presentation ended, the club used the numbered sheet to rebuild the display for Friday.
The students learned to check the date and shared-space schedule first.

slashRows.en: The art club prepared a hallway display for a Friday school event.
slashRows.jp: 美術部は金曜日の学校行事に向けて廊下の展示を準備しました。

slashRows.en: On Wednesday, a student read the calendar quickly and thought the event was Thursday.
slashRows.jp: 水曜日、一人の生徒がカレンダーを急いで見て行事は木曜日だと思いました。

slashRows.en: The club put all the pictures on the hallway wall that afternoon.
slashRows.jp: 部はその日の午後、すべての絵を廊下の壁に飾りました。

slashRows.en: A teacher then pointed out that another class needed the wall for a Thursday morning presentation.
slashRows.jp: 先生が、その壁は木曜朝に別のクラスが発表で使うと伝えました。

slashRows.en: The club checked the event calendar and confirmed Friday as its display date.
slashRows.jp: 部が行事予定を確認すると、自分たちの展示日は金曜日だと確認できました。

slashRows.en: They did not ask the other class to change its scheduled presentation.
slashRows.jp: 別のクラスに予定された発表を変えてもらうことはしませんでした。

slashRows.en: They removed the pictures, numbered their order, and stored them overnight.
slashRows.jp: 絵を外し、順番に番号を付けて一晩保管しました。

slashRows.en: After the Thursday presentation ended, the club used the numbered sheet to rebuild the display for Friday.
slashRows.jp: 木曜の発表後、番号表を使って金曜日の展示を作り直しました。

slashRows.en: The students learned to check the date and shared-space schedule first.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは、先に日付と共有場所の予定を確認すると学びました。

title: The Aquarium Feeding Mark Written in the Wrong Row
sentences: Two students took turns feeding the fish in the classroom aquarium.
On Thursday morning, Sota saw no mark in the Thursday row of the feeding chart.
He was about to feed the fish, but a fresh mark in Friday's row stopped him.
Friday had not come yet, so Sota asked Aya about the mark in the wrong row.
Aya remembered feeding the fish ten minutes earlier and confirmed the mistake.
Sota did not feed the fish a second time.
They moved the mark to Thursday and added the feeding time beside it.
From then on, the feeder said the day aloud before making a mark.
Sota learned that an impossible date can be a clue to check a record before repeating a care task.

slashRows.en: Two students took turns feeding the fish in the classroom aquarium.
slashRows.jp: 二人の生徒が交代で教室の水槽の魚に餌をやっていました。

slashRows.en: On Thursday morning, Sota saw no mark in the Thursday row of the feeding chart.
slashRows.jp: 木曜の朝、颯太は餌やり表の木曜日の欄に印がないのを見ました。

slashRows.en: He was about to feed the fish, but a fresh mark in Friday's row stopped him.
slashRows.jp: 魚に餌をやろうとしましたが、金曜日の欄の新しい印を見て手を止めました。

slashRows.en: Friday had not come yet, so Sota asked Aya about the mark in the wrong row.
slashRows.jp: 金曜日はまだなので、颯太は彩に間違った欄の印について尋ねました。

slashRows.en: Aya remembered feeding the fish ten minutes earlier and confirmed the mistake.
slashRows.jp: 彩は十分前に餌をやったことを思い出し、記入ミスを確認しました。

slashRows.en: Sota did not feed the fish a second time.
slashRows.jp: 颯太は魚に二回目の餌をやりませんでした。

slashRows.en: They moved the mark to Thursday and added the feeding time beside it.
slashRows.jp: 印を木曜日へ移し、その横に餌をやった時刻も書きました。

slashRows.en: From then on, the feeder said the day aloud before making a mark.
slashRows.jp: それ以降、餌をやる人は印を付ける前に曜日を声に出すことにしました。

slashRows.en: Sota learned that an impossible date can be a clue to check a record before repeating a care task.
slashRows.jp: 颯太は、あり得ない日付は世話を重ねる前に記録を確認する手がかりになると学びました。

title: A Choir Folder Taken to the Practice Room Next Door
sentences: The school choir practiced in Music Room A after lunch.
Practice ended, but Miki did not find the blue folder with the alto music.
Someone remembered moving two folders into Music Room B next door.
Miki checked Room B but first saw only a similar blue folder for the brass band.
She left it because its label clearly said 'Brass.'
She looked beside the piano bench and found another blue folder partly under a black case.
Its label said 'Choir Alto,' and the first page matched the song they had practiced.
Miki returned it to the choir shelf and wrote Room B on the temporary move note.
She learned to trace a moved object and check its label before taking it.

slashRows.en: The school choir practiced in Music Room A after lunch.
slashRows.jp: 合唱部は昼食後、音楽室Aで練習しました。

slashRows.en: Practice ended, but Miki did not find the blue folder with the alto music.
slashRows.jp: 練習が終わりましたが、美紀はアルトの楽譜が入った青いファイルを見つけられませんでした。

slashRows.en: Someone remembered moving two folders into Music Room B next door.
slashRows.jp: 誰かが隣の音楽室Bへ二冊のファイルを移したことを思い出しました。

slashRows.en: Miki checked Room B but first saw only a similar blue folder for the brass band.
slashRows.jp: 美紀がB室を調べると、最初に見えたのは似た青い吹奏楽部のファイルだけでした。

slashRows.en: She left it because its label clearly said 'Brass.'
slashRows.jp: 「吹奏楽」と表示されていたため、そのファイルは持ち出しませんでした。

slashRows.en: She looked beside the piano bench and found another blue folder partly under a black case.
slashRows.jp: ピアノ椅子の横を見ると、黒いケースの下に別の青いファイルが少し見えました。

slashRows.en: Its label said 'Choir Alto,' and the first page matched the song they had practiced.
slashRows.jp: 表示は「合唱アルト」で、最初のページは練習した曲と一致しました。

slashRows.en: Miki returned it to the choir shelf and wrote Room B on the temporary move note.
slashRows.jp: 美紀はファイルを合唱部の棚へ戻し、一時移動のメモにB室と書きました。

slashRows.en: She learned to trace a moved object and check its label before taking it.
slashRows.jp: 美紀は、移動先をたどり表示を確認してから物を取ると学びました。

title: The Cafeteria Portion Test after Too Much Rice Was Left
sentences: The cafeteria team noticed that many bowls still held rice after lunch on three Mondays.
At first, they thought students simply disliked Monday's main dishes.
They weighed the leftover rice and found much more waste than on Tuesday or Wednesday.
A short survey showed that most students liked the food but felt the standard rice serving was too large.
The team did not reduce every meal immediately; one week's result did not show all students.
For two weeks, one line offered a slightly smaller first serving and allowed students to ask for more.
Waste fell, while the number of students asking for a second serving stayed small.
The cafeteria then kept the smaller first portion but continued recording waste each week.
They learned that reducing food waste works better when a change is tested and students can still request enough food.

slashRows.en: The cafeteria team noticed that many bowls still held rice after lunch on three Mondays.
slashRows.jp: 給食係は三週続けて月曜日の昼食後、多くの茶わんにご飯が残っていることに気づきました。

slashRows.en: At first, they thought students simply disliked Monday's main dishes.
slashRows.jp: 最初は、月曜日の主菜が生徒に好まれていないのだと思いました。

slashRows.en: They weighed the leftover rice and found much more waste than on Tuesday or Wednesday.
slashRows.jp: 残ったご飯を量ると、火曜や水曜よりかなり多いと分かりました。

slashRows.en: A short survey showed that most students liked the food but felt the standard rice serving was too large.
slashRows.jp: 短いアンケートでは、多くの生徒が料理は好きだが標準のご飯量が多すぎると答えました。

slashRows.en: The team did not reduce every meal immediately; one week's result did not show all students.
slashRows.jp: 一週間の結果だけでは全員の様子を示せないため、すぐすべての食事量を減らしませんでした。

slashRows.en: For two weeks, one line offered a slightly smaller first serving and allowed students to ask for more.
slashRows.jp: 二週間、一つの列では最初の量を少し減らし、必要ならおかわりできるようにしました。

slashRows.en: Waste fell, while the number of students asking for a second serving stayed small.
slashRows.jp: 残飯は減り、おかわりを求める生徒数も少ないままでした。

slashRows.en: The cafeteria then kept the smaller first portion but continued recording waste each week.
slashRows.jp: そこで給食係は最初の量を少なめにしつつ、毎週残飯量を記録し続けました。

slashRows.en: They learned that reducing food waste works better when a change is tested and students can still request enough food.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは、食品ロス削減は変更を試しつつ必要量を追加できるようにするとよりよく進むと学びました。

title: Two Clubs Asked for the Same Study Room
sentences: The science club and the English club both reserved Study Room 3 for Thursday after school.
The conflict appeared because one request had been written on paper while the other had been entered online.
Science needed sinks in the room for a short experiment, while English needed a quiet place for speaking practice.
The clubs first discussed splitting the hour equally, but moving the experiment halfway through would take too long.
They checked other rooms instead of deciding that the club with the earlier message automatically won.
Room 5 had no sinks but was quiet and open for the full hour.
English moved to Room 5, and science kept Room 3 for the experiment.
The teacher then required all future reservations to be copied into one shared calendar.
The clubs learned that a fair solution should match each group's real needs and also remove the cause of the conflict.

slashRows.en: The science club and the English club both reserved Study Room 3 for Thursday after school.
slashRows.jp: 科学部と英語部がどちらも木曜放課後の第三自習室を予約していました。

slashRows.en: The conflict appeared because one request had been written on paper while the other had been entered online.
slashRows.jp: 一方は紙、もう一方はオンラインで申請したため、重複に気づきませんでした。

slashRows.en: Science needed sinks in the room for a short experiment, while English needed a quiet place for speaking practice.
slashRows.jp: 科学部は短い実験のため室内の流しを必要とし、英語部は会話練習の静かな場所を必要としていました。

slashRows.en: The clubs first discussed splitting the hour equally, but moving the experiment halfway through would take too long.
slashRows.jp: 最初は一時間を半分ずつ使う案を考えましたが、実験を途中で移すには時間がかかりすぎました。

slashRows.en: They checked other rooms instead of deciding that the club with the earlier message automatically won.
slashRows.jp: 早い申請の部が自動的に勝つと決めず、ほかの部屋も調べました。

slashRows.en: Room 5 had no sinks but was quiet and open for the full hour.
slashRows.jp: 第五教室には流しはありませんが、静かで一時間ずっと空いていました。

slashRows.en: English moved to Room 5, and science kept Room 3 for the experiment.
slashRows.jp: 英語部が第五教室へ移り、科学部は実験のため第三自習室を使いました。

slashRows.en: The teacher then required all future reservations to be copied into one shared calendar.
slashRows.jp: 先生は今後すべての予約を一つの共有カレンダーにも記録することにしました。

slashRows.en: The clubs learned that a fair solution should match each group's real needs and also remove the cause of the conflict.
slashRows.jp: 両部は、公平な解決には各班の本当の必要に合わせ、重複の原因もなくすことが大切だと学びました。

title: Rainwater Collected beside the Bicycle Parking Area
sentences: After heavy rain, students found a wide puddle beside the bicycle parking area.
Riders had to step into the water when they moved bicycles from the back row.
The environment club first suggested adding more gravel everywhere around the parking area.
Before buying anything, they watched the next rain and saw water flowing from one roof pipe toward a low corner.
They realized that covering the whole area would cost more without changing where most water arrived.
With the school manager, they cleared leaves from a nearby drain and made a shallow gravel channel from the pipe to it.
During the next storm, the channel carried most water away and the puddle became much smaller.
The club marked the remaining wet spot for another check rather than claiming the problem was completely solved.
They learned that observing how water actually moves can lead to a smaller and more useful repair.

slashRows.en: After heavy rain, students found a wide puddle beside the bicycle parking area.
slashRows.jp: 大雨の後、生徒たちは自転車置き場の横に大きな水たまりを見つけました。

slashRows.en: Riders had to step into the water when they moved bicycles from the back row.
slashRows.jp: 奥の列から自転車を出すとき、利用者は水の中へ足を入れなければなりませんでした。

slashRows.en: The environment club first suggested adding more gravel everywhere around the parking area.
slashRows.jp: 環境部は最初、自転車置き場の周り全体に砂利を増やす案を出しました。

slashRows.en: Before buying anything, they watched the next rain and saw water flowing from one roof pipe toward a low corner.
slashRows.jp: 購入前に次の雨を観察すると、一本の雨どいから低い角へ水が流れていると分かりました。

slashRows.en: They realized that covering the whole area would cost more without changing where most water arrived.
slashRows.jp: 全体を覆っても、多くの水が来る場所は変わらず費用だけ増えると気づきました。

slashRows.en: With the school manager, they cleared leaves from a nearby drain and made a shallow gravel channel from the pipe to it.
slashRows.jp: 学校管理者と一緒に近くの排水口の葉を取り、雨どいからそこへ浅い砂利の水路を作りました。

slashRows.en: During the next storm, the channel carried most water away and the puddle became much smaller.
slashRows.jp: 次の嵐では水路が大部分の水を流し、水たまりはかなり小さくなりました。

slashRows.en: The club marked the remaining wet spot for another check rather than claiming the problem was completely solved.
slashRows.jp: 部は問題が完全に解決したとせず、残った湿った場所を次の確認用に記録しました。

slashRows.en: They learned that observing how water actually moves can lead to a smaller and more useful repair.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは、水が実際にどう動くか観察すれば、より小さく効果的な改善につながると学びました。
